1	# Architecture
2	
3	Crossfoot is one Python package with a command-line entry point, files on disk, and a static results page. No
4	server, no database server, no queue. Each part below names the requirement in `.prod-build/contract.md` that forces it.
5	
6	## The idea in one paragraph
7	
8	A scanned table prints its own totals. If every cell is read into a ledger, each value can be tested twice: its
9	row has to add up to the total printed at the end of the row, and its column has to add up to the total printed
10	under the column. One wrong cell fails both sums, and the two failing sums cross at it. Crossfoot reads the scan
11	with a vision model, accepts a value only when both sums hold, re-reads the cells where they do not, and then uses
12	the closed ledger to audit a published file that was copied from the same scan.
13	
14	## Layout of the repository
15	
16	```
17	crossfoot/
18	  cli.py        command-line entry point (argparse): audit, read, verify-known, budget, site
19	  sources.py    the eight benchmark counties: scan URL, published-file URL, cache under data/ (M1, M4)
20	  render.py     pdftoppm wrapper: page -> PNG at a dpi; crops with Pillow (M1, M3)
21	  segment.py    finds blocks and column lines on a ruled page from the image itself (M1)
22	  model.py      gateway client, JSON parsing with one repair attempt, cost meter, budget guard, rate limit (M7)
23	  tracing.py    neatlogs setup and span helpers; a no-op when the key is absent (M7)
24	  layouts/
25	    matrix.py   precincts as columns, three rows per candidate, totals both ways (Panola)
26	    report.py   one precinct per page, one row per candidate with its own total (San Saba, Cottle and others)
27	    profile.py  decides which layout a county uses and tests the decision on the first pages (M1)
28	  ledger.py     SQLite ledger: cells, printed totals, checks, events; resume (M2, M6)
29	  checks.py     row sums, column sums, grand totals, grid completeness; pure functions (M2)
30	  agent.py      the investigation loop: a model chooses the next action for each open item; code enforces the rules (M3)
31	  audit.py      compares the closed ledger with the published file; classifies and settles disagreements (M4)
32	  outputs.py    county.json, findings.json, corrected CSV, report.md, the site's data bundle (M5, M8)
33	  policy.py     the one stored answer and its default (S1)
34	tests/          unit tests for checks, ledger, audit, budget, resume, agent rules; no network
35	site/           the static results page (plain HTML, CSS and JS; no build step) (M8)
36	runs/           one folder per run; small results are committed, caches are not
37	data/           downloaded scans and files; never committed
38	```
39	
40	## Inputs
41	
42	Eight Texas counties from the OpenElections project's 2024 general election benchmark. All eight scans are
43	image-only PDFs (no text layer): Cottle 12 pages, Foard 16, Jones 20, Limestone 42, Lynn 37, Panola 6, San Saba 21,
44	Scurry 38.
45	
46	- Scan: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openelections/openelections-sources-tx/master/2024/general/2024%20<County>%20County%2C%20TX%20precinct-level%20results.pdf`
47	- Published file: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openelections/openelections-data-tx/master/2024/counties/20241105__tx__general__<county>__precinct.csv`
48	  with columns `county, precinct, office, district, party, candidate, votes, absentee, early_voting, election_day`.
49	
50	## Two layouts
51	
52	**Matrix (Panola).** A landscape canvass sheet. The header row lists the precincts as columns and ends in a TOTAL
53	column. Each candidate is a block: a label at the left, three ruled rows (EARLY, ABSENTEE, PRECINCT), a row of
54	small printed totals under the columns, and a grand total under the TOTAL column. In the published file EARLY is
55	`early_voting`, ABSENTEE is `absentee`, PRECINCT is `election_day`, and the small total is `votes`.
56	Checks per block: for each precinct, early + absentee + precinct = the small total; for each row, the precinct cells
57	add to the row's TOTAL; the small totals add to the grand total.
58	
59	**Report (San Saba, Cottle and others).** One precinct per page or section. Each candidate is a row with four
60	numbers: TOTAL, Absentee, Early Voting, Election Day. Checks per row: total = absentee + early + election day.
61	Where the page prints a total for the contest, the candidates' totals have to add to it.
62	
63	`layouts/profile.py` asks the model which layout the first page shows and what the column order is, then reads the
64	first page under that layout and runs the checks. A profile under which more than a third of the sums fail is
65	rejected; the other layout is tried; if neither holds the county is reported as "layout not supported" and left alone.
66	
67	## Reading
68	
69	1. `render.py` renders a page at 200 dpi.
70	2. Matrix: `segment.py` finds the blocks as bands of ink separated by blank bands, and the column lines inside a
71	   block as columns of dark pixels that run the height of the ruled rows. Report: the page is read whole.
72	3. Matrix: each block is cut into column groups no wider than 1,500 px at 300 dpi, one model call per group; report:
73	   one page per call. The answer is strict JSON, validated (right number of columns, integers only), with one repair
74	   request. Every value comes back with the block, row kind and column it belongs to.
75	4. Which model reads a county is decided by measurement, not fixed. A sample of the first page is read with
76	   `claude-haiku`; if more than a tenth of the sample's row sums fail, the county is read with `claude-sonnet-4.6`.
77	   Measured on Panola on 11 October 2026, same code and crops: `claude-haiku` left 85 of 943 printed sums failing
78	   (44 after a 20-minute re-read loop with 565 more calls); `claude-sonnet-4.6` left 6 of 942.
79	5. The values go into the ledger as `first_read`, with the page and the pixel box of each value where it is known.
80	
81	## The ledger (`ledger.py`, SQLite, one file per run)
82	
83	- `cells(county, page, block_id, contest, candidate, row_kind, column, value, first_read, status, tries, model, x0, y0, x1, y1)`
84	  with status in `first_read | accepted | failed | cannot_verify`.
85	- `totals(county, page, block_id, direction, key, value)` for printed row totals, column totals and grand totals.
86	- `events(ts, county, kind, payload_json)` for everything the agent did, in order. The results page replays these.
87	- A county is `closed` when every sum holds and the grid has no gap, or every open cell is `cannot_verify`.
88	- Resume: on start, accepted cells are kept and only open ones are worked on.
89	
90	## Checks (`checks.py`, no model, no I/O)
91	
92	Pure functions over the ledger's rows. They return, for each sum, its terms, the printed total, the computed total
93	and pass or fail, and for each failing cell the sums that cross at it. `locate()` returns the cells that sit on a
94	failing row sum and a failing column sum at once. Grid completeness lists every precinct, contest and candidate that
95	is present in one place and absent in another.
96	
97	## The investigation loop (`agent.py`)
98	
99	Every value on a matrix sheet sits on two printed sums. A cell sits on its row and its column. The small total under
100	a column sits on that column and on the grand total (the small totals add to it). A row's printed total sits on its
101	row and on the grand total (the three row totals add to it). So one wrong value makes exactly two sums fail, and they
102	cross at it. `checks.suspects()` pairs failing sums that share one value and whose differences agree: that value is
103	the suspect, and the difference says what it would have to be. (The grand total is checked two ways, kinds `grand_col`
104	and `grand_row`. The registered-voters row of Panola sits on one sum only and cannot be located this way.)
105	
106	The loop works the sums that still fail after the first read, and later every disagreement with the published file.
107	For a located suspect it looks at the scan again: a re-read of that one value, cut at 400 dpi or more and enlarged.
108	A value changes only because a re-read of the scan gave the new value; arithmetic says where to look, never what to
109	write. What pairing cannot locate goes to the model, which is shown the failing sums and what has been tried and
110	returns one action as JSON:
111	
112	- `reread {target, dpi, model}`: a single value, a column slice or a row strip
113	- `conclude {item, verdict, reason}`: `document_inconsistent` or `cannot_verify`
114	- `ask_policy {question_id}`: use the stored answer, or the default marked as unconfirmed
115	- `done {item}`
116	
117	Rules that code enforces whatever the model says: at most six actions per item; re-reads climb one step at a time
118	(the county's reader, then `claude-sonnet-4.6`, then `claude-opus-4.6`), a step only after the one below has failed
119	to settle the value; the same target is never re-read twice with the same model and dpi; no value is accepted unless
120	both of its sums hold; a value the scan shows the same way twice while its two sums still fail is
121	`document_inconsistent` (the document disagrees with itself there) and the stored policy answer applies; a correction
122	is written only when the printed totals agree with the new value and disagree with the old one.
123	Every action and its result is an event in the ledger and a span in neatlogs.
124	
125	## The audit (`audit.py`)
126	
127	1. Load the published file. Normalise labels (case, punctuation, party suffixes, running mates).
128	2. Map the scan's contests and candidates to the file's. Exact and normalised matches first; what is left goes to
129	   the model once per county as two lists, and code checks that the answer is one-to-one and that mapped pairs have
130	   close county totals.
131	3. Compare cell by cell. A disagreement is classified:
132	   `file_row_fails_own_total`, `wrong_number`, `wrong_column`, `wrong_precinct`, `missing_row`, `extra_row`.
133	4. Settle it. If the scan's value passes both of its sums and the file's value breaks a printed total, the status is
134	   `settled_against_file`. If no printed total can decide, `cannot_verify`. If the scan's own totals disagree with
135	   its cells, `document_inconsistent`, and the stored policy answer applies.
136	5. Keep the evidence: the crop of the block, the sums with their terms, the old and the new value.
137	   Every finding carries `confirmed_by_person: false` until a person changes it.
138	
139	## Outputs (`outputs.py`)
140	
141	`runs/<run_id>/run.json` (start, end, commit, model calls, tokens, cost, counties), and per county
142	`county.json` (cells, totals, checks, events), `findings.json`, `crops/*.png`, `corrected/<published file name>`,
143	`changes.diff` and `report.md`. `crossfoot site build --run <id>` copies what the results page needs into
144	`site/data/`: `index.json`, one JSON per county, the page images that carry findings (at most 1600 px wide) and the crops.
145	
146	## Tracing and cost (`tracing.py`, `model.py`)
147	
148	`neatlogs.init(api_key=..., workflow_name="crossfoot")`; the gateway client is wrapped with `neatlogs.wrap(OpenAI(...))`.
149	A county run is a `WORKFLOW` span, the loop is an `AGENT` span, each tool is a `TOOL` span
150	(`@neatlogs.span(kind="TOOL", tool_name=...)`), tagged with run, county, page, block and cell. `neatlogs.flush()` and
151	`neatlogs.shutdown()` run at exit. The cost meter adds up each response's token usage, and `crossfoot budget` reads
152	the gateway's own figure for the key (`GET <gateway root>/key/info`, where the root is `LITELLM_BASE_URL` without
153	`/v1`). The guard refuses a call that would pass the limit.
154	
155	## The results page (`site/`)
156	
157	Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript modules, no framework and no build step, so it deploys as static files. It reads
158	`site/data/`. The scan is an image inside a container with CSS perspective; cells, sums and marks are DOM and SVG
159	elements placed in the image's own coordinates, so they tilt with it and stay real, selectable elements.
160	`UI-SPEC.md` is the specification.
161	
162	## What can fail and what happens
163	
164	| Dependency | Failure | What the program does |
165	|---|---|---|
166	| Model gateway | rate limit, timeout | waits and retries once, then marks the item cannot-verify |
167	| Model gateway | budget reached | stops before the call, writes what it has, exits with a clear message |
168	| Model answer | not valid JSON, wrong column count | one repair request, then the block is marked failed and goes to the loop |
169	| Scan or file | cannot be downloaded | that county stops with the URL; other counties continue |
170	| neatlogs | key missing or unreachable | the run continues untraced and says so on its first line |
171	| Position finding | no ruled lines | crops fall back to whole blocks and the page shows crops without cell marks |
172	
173	## Decisions
174	
175	- SQLite for the ledger, because a stopped run has to resume and the page replays events in order.
176	- A JSON action protocol for the loop instead of provider tool-calling, so it runs unchanged on any model the gateway serves.
177	- CSS 3D for the stage instead of WebGL: the sheet is the only object, text has to stay crisp and selectable, and
178	  the page has to work with the effect off.
179

1	"""Which model reads a county, decided by measurement.
2	
3	A sample (the candidate blocks of page 1 until at least SAMPLE_ROW_SUMS row sums exist) is read with the cheap model.
4	If more than a tenth of the sample's row sums fail, the county is read with the stronger model and the sample's values
5	are thrown away; otherwise the cheap model keeps the county and so does the sample. The figures of the decision are
6	written as an event and a span and printed as one line (see `matrix.read_county`).
7	"""
8	from __future__ import annotations
9	
10	SAMPLE_MODEL = "claude-haiku"
11	STRONG_MODEL = "claude-sonnet-4.6"
12	SAMPLE_ROW_SUMS = 20
13	FAIL_LINE = 0.10        # more than this share of the sample's row sums failing switches the reader
14	
15	
16	def decide(failing: int, total: int) -> dict:
17	    """The decision from the sample's figures. `total` is the number of row sums in the sample."""
18	    rate = failing / total if total else 1.0
19	    switch = total == 0 or failing * 10 > total
20	    return {"row_sums": total, "failing": failing, "rate": round(rate, 4), "line": FAIL_LINE,
21	            "sampled_with": SAMPLE_MODEL, "reader": STRONG_MODEL if switch else SAMPLE_MODEL,
22	            "kept_sample": not switch}

75	def plan_groups(edges, label_x0, total_x1, *, scale, max_w) -> list[Group]:
76	    """Cut the columns (n+1 edges) into runs whose image, with labels in the first and TOTAL in the last, fits max_w."""
77	    n = len(edges) - 1
78	    label_w = (edges[0] - label_x0) * scale
79	    total_w = (total_x1 - edges[n]) * scale
80	    out, c = [], 0
81	    while c < n:
82	        first = c == 0
83	        w = label_w if first else 0.0
84	        c1 = c
85	        while c1 < n:
86	            nw = w + (edges[c1 + 1] - edges[c1]) * scale
87	            last_extra = total_w if c1 + 1 == n else 0.0
88	            if c1 > c and nw + last_extra > max_w:
89	                break
90	            w, c1 = nw, c1 + 1
91	        last = c1 == n
92	        out.append(Group(c, c1, first, last, w + (total_w if last else 0.0)))
93	        c = c1
94	    return out

386	        from ..sources import DATA
387	        self.county, self.cols, self.root = county, list(cols), root or DATA
388	        self._pages: dict = {}
389	        self._rule_cache: dict = {}

393	        if page not in self._pages:
394	            blocks = find_blocks(page_png(self.county, page, GEO_DPI, self.root))
395	            self._pages[page] = (blocks, _edges(blocks, len(self.cols)))

398	    def _block(self, page, bid):
399	        blocks, edges = self._page(page)
400	        i = 0 if bid in ("reg", "cast") else int(bid.rsplit("-b", 1)[1])
401	        if i >= len(blocks) or edges is None:
402	            raise GeometryError(f"no column lines found for {bid} on page {page}")
403	        rows = HEADER_ROWS if bid in ("reg", "cast") else ROWS
404	        self._cur_page = page
405	        self._rules(blocks[i], edges)

408	    def _rules(self, b, edges):
409	        """y of each horizontal rule across the precinct columns inside the block's ruled height, found in the image."""
410	        key = (b.y0, b.x0)
411	        if key not in self._rule_cache:
412	            import numpy as np
413	            png = page_png(self.county, self._cur_page, GEO_DPI, self.root)
414	            with Image.open(png) as im:
415	                g = np.asarray(im.convert("L"))[b.rule_y0 - 3:b.rule_y1 + 4, edges[0]:edges[-2]]
416	            cover = (g < 110).mean(axis=1) >= 0.6
417	            ys = []
418	            for s_, e_ in segment._runs(cover):
419	                ys.append(b.rule_y0 - 3 + (s_ + e_) // 2)
420	            self._rule_cache[key] = ys
421	        return self._rule_cache[key]

423	    def _row(self, b, rows, kind):
424	        i = rows.index(kind)
425	        ys = self._rule_cache.get((b.y0, b.x0)) or []
426	        h = (b.rule_y1 - b.rule_y0) / len(rows)
427	
428	        def edge(j):    # an even split, moved onto a drawn rule when one lies within 5 px
429	            y = b.rule_y0 + j * h

1	"""Row sums, column sums and grid completeness. Pure functions: no I/O, no model.
2	
3	Inputs are plain dicts as the ledger returns them. A cell needs `page, block_id, row_kind, column, value`
4	(value None means unread). A printed total is `page, block_id, direction, key, value` with direction
5	'row' (key = row_kind), 'col' (key = column) or 'grand' (key ignored).
6	A cell is identified by the tuple (page, block_id, row_kind, column), called a cell key below.
7	"""
8	from __future__ import annotations
9	
10	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
11	
12	ROW_TOTAL_COLUMN = "TOTAL"  # a cell in this column is the row's printed total, not a term
13	
14	
15	@dataclass
16	class Check:
17	    kind: str                 # 'row' | 'col' | 'grand_col' (small totals add to the grand total) | 'grand_row' (row totals do)
18	    page: int
19	    block_id: str
20	    key: str                  # row_kind for a row sum, column for a column sum, '' for grand
21	    terms: list = field(default_factory=list)  # [(cell key, value)]
22	    printed: int | None = None
23	    computed: int | None = None  # None when a term is unread
24	    ok: bool = False
25	    printed_key: tuple | None = None   # the printed total as a value of its own: (page, block, 'row'|'col'|'grand', key)
26	    note: str = ""                     # what is special about this sum (the registered-voters row sits on one sum only)
27	
28	
29	def cell_key(c: dict) -> tuple:
30	    return (c["page"], c["block_id"], c["row_kind"], c["column"])
31	
32	
33	def _printed(totals, direction):
34	    return {(t["page"], t["block_id"], t["key"] if direction != "grand" else ""): t["value"]
35	            for t in totals if t["direction"] == direction}
36	
37	
38	ONE_SUM = "registered voters: this row has no column sums, so its values sit on one sum only"
39	
40	
41	def _make(kind, page, block, key, cells, printed, printed_key=None, note="") -> Check:
42	    terms = [(cell_key(c), c["value"]) for c in cells]
43	    computed = None if any(v is None for _, v in terms) else sum(v for _, v in terms)
44	    return Check(kind, page, block, key, terms, printed, computed, computed is not None and computed == printed,
45	                 printed_key, note)
46	
47	
48	def row_checks(cells: list[dict], totals: list[dict]) -> list[Check]:
49	    """One check per (page, block, row_kind) that has a printed row total: the row's cells must add to it."""
50	    printed = _printed(totals, "row")
51	    groups: dict = {}
52	    for c in cells:
53	        if c["column"] != ROW_TOTAL_COLUMN:
54	            groups.setdefault((c["page"], c["block_id"], c["row_kind"]), []).append(c)
55	    return [_make("row", *k, g, printed[k], (k[0], k[1], "row", k[2]), ONE_SUM if k[2] == "REGISTERED" else "")
56	            for k, g in groups.items() if k in printed]
57	
58	
59	def column_checks(cells: list[dict], totals: list[dict]) -> list[Check]:
60	    """One check per (page, block, column) that has a printed column total: the column's cells must add to it."""
61	    printed = _printed(totals, "col")
62	    groups: dict = {}
63	    for c in cells:
64	        groups.setdefault((c["page"], c["block_id"], c["column"]), []).append(c)
65	    return [_make("col", *k, g, printed[k], (k[0], k[1], "col", k[2])) for k, g in groups.items() if k in printed]
66	
67	
68	def grand_checks(totals: list[dict]) -> list[Check]:
69	    """The printed column totals of a block must add to its printed grand total (kind 'grand_col')."""
70	    grand = _printed(totals, "grand")
71	    out = []
72	    for (page, block, _), g in grand.items():
73	        cols = [t for t in totals if t["direction"] == "col" and t["page"] == page and t["block_id"] == block]
74	        terms = [((page, block, "col", t["key"]), t["value"]) for t in cols]
75	        comp = sum(v for _, v in terms)
76	        out.append(Check("grand_col", page, block, "", terms, g, comp, comp == g, (page, block, "grand", "")))
77	    return out
78	
79	
80	def grand_row_checks(totals: list[dict]) -> list[Check]:
81	    """The printed row totals of a block must add to its printed grand total (kind 'grand_row'). The registered-voters
82	    row is not a term: it is not a count of ballots."""
83	    grand = _printed(totals, "grand")
84	    out = []
85	    for (page, block, _), g in grand.items():
86	        rows = [t for t in totals if t["direction"] == "row" and t["page"] == page and t["block_id"] == block and
87	                t["key"] != "REGISTERED"]
88	        if not rows:
89	            continue
90	        terms = [((page, block, "row", t["key"]), t["value"]) for t in rows]
91	        comp = sum(v for _, v in terms)
92	        out.append(Check("grand_row", page, block, "", terms, g, comp, comp == g, (page, block, "grand", "")))
93	    return out
94

96	def grid_gaps(cells: list[dict]) -> list[tuple]:
97	    """Cell keys that are absent or unread where the block's grid says they should be.
98	
99	    Within a block the grid is every row_kind crossed with every column that appears in it.
100	    Returns sorted (page, block_id, row_kind, column) tuples.
101	    """
102	    blocks: dict = {}
103	    for c in cells:
104	        b = blocks.setdefault((c["page"], c["block_id"]), {"rows": set(), "cols": set(), "have": set()})
105	        b["rows"].add(c["row_kind"]); b["cols"].add(c["column"])
106	        if c["value"] is not None:
107	            b["have"].add((c["row_kind"], c["column"]))
108	    return sorted((p, bid, r, col) for (p, bid), b in blocks.items()
109	                  for r in b["rows"] for col in b["cols"] if (r, col) not in b["have"])
110	
111	
112	def locate(rows: list[Check], cols: list[Check]) -> list[tuple]:
113	    """Cell keys that sit on a failing row sum and on a failing column sum at once."""
114	    bad_rows = {k for ch in rows if not ch.ok for k, _ in ch.terms}
115	    bad_cols = {k for ch in cols if not ch.ok for k, _ in ch.terms}
116	    return sorted(bad_rows & bad_cols)
117	
118	
119	def all_checks(cells: list[dict], totals: list[dict]) -> list[Check]:
120	    return row_checks(cells, totals) + column_checks(cells, totals) + grand_checks(totals) + grand_row_checks(totals)
121

123	@dataclass
124	class Suspect:
125	    entity: tuple     # a cell key (page, block, row_kind, column) or a printed total (page, block, 'row'|'col'|'grand', key)
126	    read: int         # the value now in the ledger
127	    would_be: int     # the value both of its sums need
128	    error: int        # read - would_be
129	    sums: tuple       # the two failing Checks it sits on
130	
131	
132	@dataclass
133	class Located:
134	    suspects: list = field(default_factory=list)
135	    unlocated: list = field(default_factory=list)   # [(Check, why)]: failing sums no single value explains
136	
137	
138	def suspects(chs: list[Check]) -> Located:
139	    """Pair failing sums. A value that sits on exactly two failing sums, and is off by the same amount on both (the sign
140	    its place in each sum gives), is a suspect, and the value both sums need is `would_be`. A value read too high by e
141	    makes a sum it is a term of too high by e, and a sum it is the printed total of too low by e. Pure arithmetic:
142	    it says where to look, never what to write. A failing sum that no unique suspect explains is `unlocated`, with the
143	    reason (an unread term, one sum only, more than one candidate, or differences that do not pair)."""
144	    failing = [c for c in chs if not c.ok]
145	    out = Located()
146	    on: dict = {}                                  # entity -> [(Check, error it implies, value)]
147	    unread = []
148	    for c in failing:
149	        if c.computed is None or c.printed is None:
150	            unread.append(c)
151	            continue
152	        d = c.computed - c.printed
153	        for k, v in c.terms:
154	            on.setdefault(k, []).append((c, d, v))
155	        if c.printed_key is not None:
156	            on.setdefault(c.printed_key, []).append((c, -d, c.printed))
157	    cand = []
158	    for e, lst in on.items():
159	        if len(lst) == 2 and lst[0][1] == lst[1][1] != 0 and lst[0][2] - lst[0][1] >= 0:
160	            cand.append(Suspect(e, lst[0][2], lst[0][2] - lst[0][1], lst[0][1], (lst[0][0], lst[1][0])))
161	    uses: dict = {}
162	    for s in cand:
163	        for c in s.sums:
164	            uses[id(c)] = uses.get(id(c), 0) + 1
165	    out.suspects = [s for s in cand if all(uses[id(c)] == 1 for c in s.sums)]
166	    explained = {id(c) for s in out.suspects for c in s.sums}
167	    for c in failing:
168	        if id(c) in explained:
169	            continue
170	        if c in unread:
171	            why = "a term is unread"
172	        elif c.note:
173	            why = f"one sum only: {c.note}"
174	        elif uses.get(id(c), 0) > 1:
175	            why = "more than one value could be the one: several pairs of failing sums agree"
176	        else:
177	            why = "its difference cannot be paired with another failing sum (two or more wrong values may share it)"
178	        out.unlocated.append((c, why))
179	    return out
180	
181	
182	def crossing(cells: list[dict], totals: list[dict]) -> dict:
183	    """For each cell key, the row and column checks it sits on (a cell on no printed sum maps to an empty list)."""
184	    on: dict = {cell_key(c): [] for c in cells if c["column"] != ROW_TOTAL_COLUMN}
185	    for ch in row_checks(cells, totals) + column_checks(cells, totals):
186	        for k, _ in ch.terms:
187	            on[k].append(ch)
188	    return on

283	    by = {f["id"]: f for f in d["findings"]}
284	    L += ["## Groups", ""]

2	from __future__ import annotations
3	
4	import json
5	import sqlite3
6	import time
7	from pathlib import Path
8	
9	SCHEMA = """
10	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS cells(
11	  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, county TEXT, page INTEGER, block_id TEXT, contest TEXT, candidate TEXT,
12	  row_kind TEXT, column TEXT, value INTEGER, first_read INTEGER, status TEXT DEFAULT 'first_read',
13	  tries INTEGER DEFAULT 0, model TEXT, x0 INTEGER, y0 INTEGER, x1 INTEGER, y1 INTEGER, reason TEXT,
14	  UNIQUE(county, page, block_id, row_kind, column));
15	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS totals(
16	  county TEXT, page INTEGER, block_id TEXT, direction TEXT, key TEXT, value INTEGER,
17	  UNIQUE(county, page, block_id, direction, key));
18	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS verdicts(
19	  county TEXT, sum_id TEXT, page INTEGER, block_id TEXT, verdict TEXT, reason TEXT, entity TEXT,
20	  UNIQUE(county, sum_id));
21	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS events(
22	  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, ts REAL, county TEXT, kind TEXT, payload_json TEXT);
23	"""
24	STATUSES = ("first_read", "accepted", "failed", "cannot_verify", "document_inconsistent")
25	VERDICTS = ("document_inconsistent", "cannot_verify")
26	
27	
28	class Ledger:
29	    """One SQLite file. Cells are keyed by (county, page, block_id, row_kind, column)."""
30	
31	    def __init__(self, path: str | Path = ":memory:"):
32	        self.db = sqlite3.connect(str(path))
33	        self.db.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
34	        self.db.executescript(SCHEMA)
35	        if "reason" not in {r["name"] for r in self.db.execute("PRAGMA table_info(cells)")}:
36	            self.db.execute("ALTER TABLE cells ADD COLUMN reason TEXT")  # ledgers made before the loop existed
37	
38	    def close(self):
39	        self.db.close()
40	
41	    def put_cell(self, county, page, block_id, row_kind, column, value, *, contest=None, candidate=None,
42	                 model=None, box=(None, None, None, None)):
43	        """Insert a first read, or re-read an open cell. An accepted cell is never overwritten (resume)."""
44	        self.db.execute(
45	            "INSERT INTO cells(county,page,block_id,contest,candidate,row_kind,column,value,first_read,model,x0,y0,x1,y1)"
46	            " VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)"
47	            " ON CONFLICT(county,page,block_id,row_kind,column) DO UPDATE SET value=excluded.value,"
48	            " tries=tries+1, model=excluded.model WHERE status!='accepted'",
49	            (county, page, block_id, contest, candidate, row_kind, column, value, value, model, *box))
50	        self.db.commit()
51	
52	    def set_status(self, county, page, block_id, row_kind, column, status, reason=None):
53	        if status not in STATUSES:
54	            raise ValueError(f"unknown status {status!r}")
55	        self.db.execute("UPDATE cells SET status=?, reason=? WHERE county=? AND page=? AND block_id=? AND row_kind=? "
56	                        "AND column=?", (status, reason, county, page, block_id, row_kind, column))
57	        self.db.commit()
58	
59	    def reread_cell(self, county, page, block_id, row_kind, column, value, model=None):
60	        """Record one re-read of a cell: tries goes up by one, the value is the one kept, the model only if it changed it."""
61	        self.db.execute("UPDATE cells SET value=?, tries=tries+1, model=COALESCE(?, model) WHERE county=? AND page=? "
62	                        "AND block_id=? AND row_kind=? AND column=? AND status!='accepted'",
63	                        (value, model, county, page, block_id, row_kind, column))
64	        self.db.commit()
65	
66	    def set_box(self, county, page, block_id, row_kind, column, box):
67	        self.db.execute("UPDATE cells SET x0=?, y0=?, x1=?, y1=? WHERE county=? AND page=? AND block_id=? AND row_kind=? "
68	                        "AND column=?", (*box, county, page, block_id, row_kind, column))
69	        self.db.commit()
70	
71	    def set_value(self, county, page, block_id, row_kind, column, value, model=None):
72	        """Write a value the audit's re-read showed (an accepted cell included); the caller sets the status after."""
73	        self.db.execute("UPDATE cells SET value=?, tries=tries+1, model=COALESCE(?, model) WHERE county=? AND page=? "
74	                        "AND block_id=? AND row_kind=? AND column=?",
75	                        (value, model, county, page, block_id, row_kind, column))
76	        self.db.commit()
77	
78	    def put_total(self, county, page, block_id, direction, key, value):
79	        self.db.execute("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO totals VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?)",
80	                        (county, page, block_id, direction, key, value))
81	        self.db.commit()
82	
83	    def set_verdict(self, county, sum_id, page, block_id, verdict, reason, entity=None):
84	        """A failing sum that was worked and could not be made to hold: its verdict and why. One per sum."""
85	        if verdict not in VERDICTS:
86	            raise ValueError(f"unknown verdict {verdict!r}")
87	        self.db.execute("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO verdicts VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?,?)",
88	                        (county, sum_id, page, block_id, verdict, reason, json.dumps(entity) if entity else None))
89	        self.db.commit()
90	
91	    def verdicts(self, county=None) -> list[dict]:
92	        q, a = "SELECT * FROM verdicts", []
93	        if county:
94	            q += " WHERE county=?"; a.append(county)
95	        return [dict(r) for r in self.db.execute(q, a)]
96	
97	    def clear_values(self, county):
98	        """Forget every cell and printed total of a county (the sample of a read that chose another reader). Events stay."""
99	        self.db.execute("DELETE FROM cells WHERE county=?", (county,))
100	        self.db.execute("DELETE FROM totals WHERE county=?", (county,))
101	        self.db.commit()
102	
103	    def event(self, county, kind, payload=None):
104	        self.db.execute("INSERT INTO events(ts,county,kind,payload_json) VALUES(?,?,?,?)",
105	                        (time.time(), county, kind, json.dumps(payload or {})))
106	        self.db.commit()
107	
108	    def cells(self, county=None, status=None) -> list[dict]:
109	        q, a = "SELECT * FROM cells WHERE 1=1", []
110	        if county:
111	            q += " AND county=?"; a.append(county)
112	        if status:
113	            q += " AND status=?"; a.append(status)
114	        return [dict(r) for r in self.db.execute(q + " ORDER BY id", a)]
115	
116	    def totals(self, county=None) -> list[dict]:
117	        q, a = "SELECT * FROM totals", []
118	        if county:
119	            q += " WHERE county=?"; a.append(county)
120	        return [dict(r) for r in self.db.execute(q, a)]
121	
122	    def events(self, county=None) -> list[dict]:
123	        q, a = "SELECT * FROM events", []
124	        if county:
125	            q += " WHERE county=?"; a.append(county)
126	        return [dict(r) for r in self.db.execute(q + " ORDER BY id", a)]
127	
128	    def open_cells(self, county=None) -> list[dict]:
129	        """Cells that still need work: first_read or failed."""
130	        return [c for c in self.cells(county) if c["status"] in ("first_read", "failed")]

"""Report layout (San Saba, Cottle and others): one precinct per section, one row per candidate with four numbers.

Reading: the county's layout is decided from its first page (`profile.decide_layout`); the first page is read under that
decision and the decision is thrown away if more than a third of its row sums fail. The same sample chooses the reader
(`profile.decide`). One page per model call at 200 dpi, strict JSON, one repair request.

The ledger: a cell is (page, block, row, column). A block is one contest on one precinct, `block_id` "<precinct key>|<n>"
(a contest that runs over a page break is one block: its cells carry different pages and the same block id); the Statistics
rows "Ballots Cast - Total" and "Ballots Cast - Blank" are blocks of their own, named as the published file names them.
`row_kind` is the row's label as printed, `column` is total | absentee | early | election_day. A cell's box is the row's
strip of the page at 200 dpi ([0, y - 20, x_right, y + 20]; y is the model's own estimate, so the box is approximate and
re-read crops are cut with generous padding).

Checks (`checks.report_checks`): each row's total = absentee + early voting + election day; where a contest prints a total
row ("Total Votes Cast", "Cast Votes"), the candidates' figures in a column add to that row's figure in the column. A value
sits on its row's own sum, and, only where the page prints a contest total, on the column's sum too.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
import subprocess
import time
from pathlib import Path

from PIL import Image

from .. import agent, checks, tracing
from ..model import BudgetExceeded
from ..render import page_png
from . import profile

COLS = checks.REPORT_COLS
HALF_ROW = 20          # half the height of a row's box, pixels at 200 dpi
ROW_PAD = 60           # a re-read crop reaches this far above and below the row's centre, pixels at 200 dpi
GEO_DPI = 200
MAX_ACTIONS = agent.MAX_ACTIONS
NOTE_NO_TOTALS = "nothing on this scan can be cross-checked; left as published"


# ---- names: both sides are normalised before they are compared ---------------------------------------------------------

def precinct_key(name) -> str:
    """"PRECINCT 101", "Precinct 101" and "101" are one precinct; so are "Precinct 2A", "2A" and "02a"."""
    s = re.sub(r"\b(?:precinct|pct)\b", " ", str(name or ""), flags=re.I)
    s = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]", "", s.lower())
    return re.sub(r"^0+(?=\d)", "", s)


def contest_canon(label) -> str:
    """A contest's name with the scan's and the file's spellings made one: "Pl 2" = "PI 2", "Dist" = "District" (the word
    is dropped on both sides)."""
    s = re.sub(r"\b(?:district|dist)\b", " ", str(label or "").lower())
    s = re.sub(r"\bp[il](?=\s*\d)", "pl", s)
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]", "", s)


_PARTY = re.compile(r"^(REP|DEM|LIB|GRN|IND|NPA|UNA|NON)\s+(.+)$")
_WRITE_IN = ("writeintotals", "writeintotal", "writeins", "writein")


def split_label(label) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """(party, name) of a row label as printed: "REP Donald J. Trump/JD Vance" -> ("REP", "Donald J. Trump"). A write-in
    row is "Write-ins" as the published file names it."""
    s = " ".join(str(label or "").split())
    if re.sub(r"[^a-z]", "", s.lower()) in _WRITE_IN:
        return "", "Write-ins"
    m = _PARTY.match(s)
    party, rest = (m.group(1), m.group(2)) if m else ("", s)
    return party, rest.split("/")[0].strip()


# ---- the model's answers --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

PAGE_PROMPT = """TASK: page.
This image is one page of a scanned election results report (one precinct per section). At the top left, below the
report's title lines, the precinct's name is printed alone. A Statistics block may follow, then one block per contest: a
heading, "Vote For 1", then one row per candidate. Each row has a label and four numbers under the headings, left to
right: {order}. Ignore any percentage columns.
Answer with strict JSON only, no prose:
{{"precinct": "<the precinct name as printed>",
 "contests": [{{"name": "<the contest heading as printed; \\"Statistics\\" for the Statistics block>",
               "continued": <true if this block carries on a contest from the previous page (no heading, or a heading marked
                             as continued), else false>,
               "rows": [{{"label": "<the row label exactly as printed, party prefix included>",
                         "total": <integer or null>, "absentee": <integer or null>, "early": <integer or null>,
                         "election_day": <integer or null>,
                         "y": <the row's vertical position as a number from 0 (top of the page) to 1000 (bottom)>}}]}}]}}
In the Statistics block give only the rows "Ballots Cast - Total" and "Ballots Cast - Blank". Include every row of every
contest, including "Write-In Totals", "Total Votes Cast", "Cast Votes", "Overvotes" and "Undervotes" rows where printed.
Use null for a number that is not printed. Read the digits exactly as printed; do not correct or add anything up."""

ROW_PROMPT = """TASK: row.
This image is a crop of one row of a scanned election results report. The row to read is the one whose label reads
"{label}"; rows above or below it may show at the edges, ignore them. The row has up to four numbers under the headings,
left to right: {order}. Ignore any percentage.
Answer with strict JSON only: {{"total": <integer or null>, "absentee": <integer or null>, "early": <integer or null>,
"election_day": <integer or null>}}. Use null for a number that is not printed. Read the digits exactly as printed; do not
correct or add anything up."""

_NAMES = {"total": "TOTAL", "absentee": "Absentee", "early": "Early Voting", "election_day": "Election Day"}


def order_text(order) -> str:
    return ", ".join(_NAMES[c] for c in order)


def _int_or_none(v, what):
    if v is None or (isinstance(v, int) and not isinstance(v, bool)):
        return v
    raise ValueError(f"{what} must be an integer or null, got {v!r}")


def page_validator(d):
    if not isinstance(d, dict):
        raise ValueError("answer must be an object")
    p = d.get("precinct")
    if not isinstance(p, str) or not p.strip():
        raise ValueError('"precinct" must be the precinct name as a non-empty string')
    d["precinct"] = p.strip()
    cs = d.get("contests")
    if not isinstance(cs, list):
        raise ValueError('"contests" must be a list')
    for c in cs:
        if not isinstance(c, dict) or not isinstance(c.get("name", ""), str) or not isinstance(c.get("rows"), list):
            raise ValueError('each contest needs a "name" string and a "rows" list')
        c["continued"] = bool(c.get("continued"))
        for r in c["rows"]:
            if not isinstance(r, dict) or not isinstance(r.get("label"), str) or not r["label"].strip():
                raise ValueError('each row needs a "label" string')
            for col in COLS:
                _int_or_none(r.get(col), f"{col} of {r['label']!r}")
            y = r.get("y")
            if isinstance(y, bool) or not isinstance(y, (int, float)) or not 0 <= y <= 1000:
                raise ValueError(f'"y" of {r["label"]!r} must be a number from 0 to 1000')


def row_validator(d):
    if not isinstance(d, dict):
        raise ValueError("answer must be an object")
    for col in COLS:
        if col not in d:
            raise ValueError(f'"{col}" is missing')
        _int_or_none(d[col], col)


# ---- the page into the ledger ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

class State:
    def __init__(self):
        self.names: dict = {}      # precinct key -> name as printed
        self.count: dict = {}      # precinct key -> contests so far
        self.last: dict = {}       # precinct key -> (contest key, block id, contest name)
        self.labels: set = set()   # (block, row label) already stored


def ink_right(png, margin=40) -> int:
    """The right edge of the table on a page, from the middle of the page itself: the last column with ink, plus a margin."""
    import numpy as np
    with Image.open(png) as im:
        g = np.asarray(im.convert("L"))
    h, w = g.shape
    idx = np.nonzero((g[int(h * .25):int(h * .75)] < 128).sum(axis=0) >= 3)[0]
    return int(min(w, idx.max() + margin)) if len(idx) else int(w)


def store_page(led, county, page, ans, st: State, *, model, size, x_right) -> int:
    """Put one page's answer into the ledger as first reads. Returns the number of cells stored."""
    w, h = size
    pk = precinct_key(ans["precinct"])
    st.names.setdefault(pk, ans["precinct"])
    n = 0

    def put_row(block, contest, r):
        nonlocal n
        label = " ".join(r["label"].split())
        if (block, label) in st.labels:
            label += " (2)"
        st.labels.add((block, label))
        yp = float(r["y"]) / 1000 * h
        box = (0, max(0, round(yp - HALF_ROW)), x_right, min(h, round(yp + HALF_ROW)))
        for col in COLS:
            if r.get(col) is not None:
                led.put_cell(county, page, block, label, col, r[col], contest=contest, candidate=label, model=model, box=box)
                n += 1

    for i, c in enumerate(ans["contests"]):
        name = c.get("name", "").strip()
        if name.lower().startswith("statistics"):
            for r in c["rows"]:
                low = r["label"].lower()
                if "ballots cast" not in low:
                    continue
                blank = "blank" in low
                put_row(f"{pk}|s{'b' if blank else 't'}", "Ballots Cast Blank" if blank else "Ballots Cast", r)
            continue
        key, last = contest_canon(name), st.last.get(pk)
        if last and (c["continued"] or not name or (i == 0 and last[0] == key)):
            block, cname = last[1], last[2]
        else:
            st.count[pk] = st.count.get(pk, 0) + 1
            block, cname = f"{pk}|{st.count[pk]}", name or "(no heading)"
            st.last[pk] = (key, block, cname)
        for r in c["rows"]:
            put_row(block, cname, r)
    return n


# ---- reading a county --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def page_count(county, root=None) -> int:
    from ..sources import DATA, scan_path
    out = subprocess.run(["pdfinfo", str(scan_path(county, root or DATA))], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
    return int(re.search(r"^Pages:\s+(\d+)", out, re.M).group(1))

def steps(reader) -> list[tuple[str, int]]:
    """The (model, dpi) of each re-read of a row, weakest first: the county's reader at 300 and 400 dpi, then
    claude-sonnet-4.6 at 400 and 500, then claude-opus-4.6 at 500 and 600. At most six; none repeats."""
    lad = agent.ladder_for(reader)
    out: list = []
    for i, d in enumerate((300, 400, 400, 500, 500, 600)):
        s = (lad[min(i // 2, len(lad) - 1)], d)
        if s not in out:
            out.append(s)
    return out


def derive_status(led, county) -> list[dict]:
    """accepted iff the cell sits on at least one printed sum and every one holds; final statuses stay."""
    cells = led.cells(county)
    on = checks.report_crossing(cells)
    out = []
    for c in cells:
        if c["status"] in agent.FINAL:
            continue
        cs = on.get(checks.cell_key(c), [])
        new = "accepted" if cs and all(x.ok for x in cs) else ("failed" if c["status"] == "failed" else "first_read")
        if new != c["status"]:
            led.set_status(county, c["page"], c["block_id"], c["row_kind"], c["column"], new)
            out.append({"cell": list(checks.cell_key(c)), "old": c["status"], "new": new})
    return out


def _holding(cells, page, block, label) -> int:
    """How many printed sums through the row (its own, and the contest's columns) hold."""
    keys = {(page, block, label, col) for col in COLS}
    return sum(ch.ok for ch in checks.report_checks(cells)
               if any(k in keys for k, _ in ch.terms) or ch.printed_key in keys)


def _vals(cells, page, block, label) -> dict:
    return {c["column"]: c["value"] for c in cells if (c["page"], c["block_id"], c["row_kind"]) == (page, block, label)}


class Closer:
    def __init__(self, county, gw, led, geo, *, reader, run_id="", log=print, crop_dir=None, order=COLS):
        self.county, self.gw, self.led, self.geo, self.run_id, self.log = county, gw, led, geo, run_id, log
        self.reader = agent.norm(reader or getattr(gw, "model", None) or agent.HAIKU)
        self.steps = steps(self.reader)
        self.order = list(order)
        self.crop_dir = Path(crop_dir) if crop_dir else Path("runs") / run_id / "crops"
        self.n_crops = 0
        self.rereads = 0

    def ev(self, kind, **payload):
        self.led.event(self.county, kind, payload)

    def box_of(self, page, block, label):
        c = next((c for c in self.led.cells(self.county)
                  if (c["page"], c["block_id"], c["row_kind"]) == (page, block, label) and c["x0"] is not None), None)
        return [c["x0"], c["y0"], c["x1"], c["y1"]] if c else None

    def reread(self, item, page, block, label, step) -> dict | None:
        """One action: the row's strip at the step's dpi with the step's model. Keeps the new reading only if more of the
        sums through the row hold with it. Returns {values, kept, model, dpi} or None when no crop could be cut."""
        model, dpi = self.steps[step]
        box = self.box_of(page, block, label)
        self.n_crops += 1
        dest = self.crop_dir / f"reread-{self.n_crops:04d}-{block.replace('|', '-')}.png"
        try:
            if box is None:
                raise ValueError("the row has no box on the page")
            path = self.geo.crop_row(page, box, dpi, dest)
        except Exception as e:
            self.ev("refused", item=item, target=[page, block, label], reason=f"no crop: {str(e)[:120]}")
            return None
        with tracing.trace("reread_row", kind="TOOL", run=self.run_id, county=self.county, page=page, block=block,
                           row=label, dpi=dpi, model=model):
            ans = self.gw.ask_json(ROW_PROMPT.format(label=label, order=order_text(self.order)), path,
                                   validate=row_validator, model=model)
        self.rereads += 1
        cells = self.led.cells(self.county)
        old = _vals(cells, page, block, label)
        new = {c: ans[c] for c in COLS if c in old and ans[c] is not None}
        trial = [dict(c, value=new.get(c["column"], c["value"])) if (c["page"], c["block_id"], c["row_kind"]) ==
                 (page, block, label) else c for c in cells]
        kept = _holding(trial, page, block, label) > _holding(cells, page, block, label)
        for col, v in (new if kept else {}).items():
            self.led.reread_cell(self.county, page, block, label, col, v, model)
        derive = derive_status(self.led, self.county)
        self.ev("reread", item=item, page=page, block=block, row=label, model=model, dpi=dpi, ladder_step=step,
                crop=str(path), box=box, old=old, reading={c: ans[c] for c in COLS}, kept="new" if kept else "old")
        if derive:
            self.ev("status_change", changes=derive)
        return {"values": tuple(ans[c] for c in COLS), "kept": kept, "model": model, "dpi": dpi}

    def verdict(self, ch, verdict, reason):
        self.led.set_verdict(self.county, agent.sum_id(ch), ch.page, ch.block_id, verdict, reason)
        keys = {k for k, _ in ch.terms} | ({ch.printed_key} if ch.printed_key else set())
        for c in self.led.cells(self.county):
            if checks.cell_key(c) in keys and c["status"] not in agent.FINAL and c["status"] != "accepted":
                self.led.set_status(self.county, c["page"], c["block_id"], c["row_kind"], c["column"], verdict, reason)
        self.ev("verdict", sums=[agent.sum_id(ch)], verdict=verdict, reason=reason)

    def find(self, kind, page, block, key):
        return next((c for c in checks.report_checks(self.led.cells(self.county))
                     if (c.kind, c.page, c.block_id, c.key) == (kind, page, block, key)), None)

    def work_row(self, ch):
        item = agent.sum_id(ch)
        self.ev("item_start", item=item, page=ch.page, block=ch.block_id)
        readings, actions = [], 0
        for step in range(len(self.steps)):
            if actions >= MAX_ACTIONS:
                break
            actions += 1
            r = self.reread(item, ch.page, ch.block_id, ch.key, step)
            if r is None:
                break
            me = self.find(ch.kind, ch.page, ch.block_id, ch.key)
            if me is None or me.ok:
                self.ev("item_end", item=item, result="holds")
                return
            if r["values"] in [v for _, _, v in readings]:
                me = self.find(ch.kind, ch.page, ch.block_id, ch.key)
                parts = " + ".join(str(v) for _, v in me.terms)
                self.verdict(me, "document_inconsistent",
                             f"the scan shows {r['values']} (total, absentee, early voting, election day) on {len(readings) + 1} "
                             f"re-reads ({', '.join(f'{m} at {d} dpi' for m, d, _ in readings)}, and {r['model']} at "
                             f"{r['dpi']} dpi), and the row's own sum still fails: {parts} = {me.computed}, printed "
                             f"{me.printed}. The document disagrees with itself.")
                self.ev("item_end", item=item, result="document_inconsistent")
                return
            readings.append((r["model"], r["dpi"], r["values"]))
        me = self.find(ch.kind, ch.page, ch.block_id, ch.key) or ch
        gave = "; ".join(f"{m} at {d} dpi: {v}" for m, d, v in readings) or "no re-read could be made"
        self.verdict(me, "cannot_verify",
                     f"{actions} re-read(s) did not make the row's sum hold ({gave}); the row adds to {me.computed}, "
                     f"printed {me.printed}")
        self.ev("item_end", item=item, result="cannot_verify")

    def work_contest(self, ch):
        item = agent.sum_id(ch)
        self.ev("item_start", item=item, page=ch.page, block=ch.block_id)
        rows = []
        for c in self.led.cells(self.county):
            k = (c["page"], c["block_id"], c["row_kind"])
            if c["block_id"] == ch.block_id and checks.row_label_kind(c["row_kind"]) != "skip" and k not in rows:
                rows.append(k)
        rows.sort(key=lambda k: checks.row_label_kind(k[2]) == "total")      # the candidates first, the contest total last
        actions = 0
        for step in range(len(self.steps)):
            for page, block, label in rows:
                if actions >= MAX_ACTIONS:
                    break
                actions += 1
                self.reread(item, page, block, label, step)
                me = self.find(ch.kind, ch.page, ch.block_id, ch.key)
                if me is None or me.ok:
                    self.ev("item_end", item=item, result="holds")
                    return
            if actions >= MAX_ACTIONS:
                break
        me = self.find(ch.kind, ch.page, ch.block_id, ch.key) or ch
        self.verdict(me, "cannot_verify",
                     f"{actions} re-read(s) of the rows of this contest did not make the {ch.key} column hold: the "
                     f"candidates add to {me.computed}, the contest total prints {me.printed}")
        self.ev("item_end", item=item, result="cannot_verify")


def finalize(led, county) -> list[dict]:
    """Every cell ends accepted, document_inconsistent or cannot_verify: a cell on no printed sum is cannot_verify; a cell on
    a failing sum takes that sum's verdict. A failing sum without a verdict gets one. Safe to run again."""
    cells = led.cells(county)
    on = checks.report_crossing(cells)
    vs = {v["sum_id"]: v for v in led.verdicts(county)}
    for chs in on.values():
        for ch in chs:
            if not ch.ok and agent.sum_id(ch) not in vs:
                why = "the sum was not worked: the run stopped first"
                led.set_verdict(county, agent.sum_id(ch), ch.page, ch.block_id, "cannot_verify", why)
                vs[agent.sum_id(ch)] = {"verdict": "cannot_verify", "reason": why}
    out = []
    for c in cells:
        if c["status"] in ("accepted", *agent.FINAL):
            continue
        cs = on.get(checks.cell_key(c), [])
        mine = [vs[agent.sum_id(x)] for x in cs if not x.ok]
        if not cs:
            new, why = "cannot_verify", "no printed sum covers this value"
        elif mine:
            v = next((x for x in mine if x["verdict"] == "document_inconsistent"), mine[0])
            new, why = v["verdict"], v["reason"]
        else:
            continue
        led.set_status(county, c["page"], c["block_id"], c["row_kind"], c["column"], new, why)
        out.append({"cell": list(checks.cell_key(c)), "old": c["status"], "new": new, "reason": why})
    if out:
        led.event(county, "status_change", {"changes": out})
    return out
